findings.reason: Confirmed. QT.0's requires in data/atlas.json are exactly ['FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.0','FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4'], with no GeometricTopology prerequisite, and the two stage edges into QT.0 come from LI.0 and LI.4 alone. The GeometricTopology README's Layer 4 does own knot and link presentations carrying orientation and framing, Reidemeister moves and the geometric-to-diagram correspondence, and Layer 5 surgery on framed links. The five Tau Ceti declarations cited (PDCode/Basic.lean:129 for the framing integers, GaussCode/FramedUnbased.lean:25, Markov.lean:112, SmoothLink/Basic.lean:61, SpecificGroups/Braid.lean:97) all exist at f790474 and say what the finding says. PROTOCOL section 15 gives one owner per piece of mathematics, so the duplication is real and the import is the right fix.

Confirmed. The distinction is the substance of Habiro's paper: J_M is defined from an algebraically split ±1-framed (admissible) surgery presentation, and its independence needs the refined Kirby calculus for admissible links (Hoste moves), because an ordinary Kirby move leaves the admissible class. QT.3's 'independence under Kirby moves' is therefore not the statement that can be proved, and no stage names the refined theorem. I read the Habiro e-print (math/0605314v1, the source the roadmap declares) for the shape of the argument and found nothing that weakens the finding.

Confirmed. The roadmap's own declared source builds J_M from U_h(sl2) as a ribbon Hopf algebra, the universal sl2 invariant of bottom tangles valued in completed tensor powers of the even integral form, and the twist element omega in P-hat, none of which QT.1-QT.3 name; what QT.1 plans (ribbon categories, U_q(sl2) modules, the semisimplified root-of-unity category) is the Reshetikhin-Turaev route to tau_zeta, a different construction. The three Mathlib citations resolve at the pin (Braided/Basic.lean:50 BraidedCategory, Rigid/Basic.lean:77 ExactPairing, HopfAlgebra/Basic.lean:65), so the duplication half is right too.

Confirmed. QT.1 constructs only U_q(sl2), and a search of all 1968 atlas stage descriptions finds no quantum group of a general simple Lie algebra, no Drinfeld-Jimbo presentation and no Lusztig or De Concini-Procesi integral form. The Habiro-Le construction that QT.4's general-Lie-type target names therefore has no supplier.

Confirmed. GeometricTopology Layer 4's text does own the Jones polynomial 'via the Kauffman bracket with t = A^-4 and V_unknot = 1', with two algorithms and an agreement theorem, and TauCeti/KnotTheory/TemperleyLieb.lean:107 exists at the pin. QT.2 neither imports it nor plans the comparison, so the two normalisations would stand side by side unreconciled.

Confirmed. I read the requires directly: QT.5 requires ['ArithmeticQuantumTopology:QT.0','K3BlochGroups:V.3','K3BlochGroups:V.5'], so both (i) and (ii) are as stated. (iv) is right as well: Polylogarithms P.1 owns the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm and P.2 'the weight-two regulator ... and hyperbolic' volume calculation, and K3BlochGroups has no regulator stage.

Confirmed. P.2's stage text places Bloch's hyperbolic-volume calculation in the weight-two regulator, and QT.5 plans the same identity again as the comparison of the real regulator with volume. AUDIT-30 has a result file and flags the pair; RS-10, the only proposal that touches this family, is not in data/restructure and its review REV-RS-10 records 'needs changes', so nothing resolves it.

Confirmed. A search of every atlas stage description finds no ideal triangulation, no cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold and no Thurston gluing or completeness equations, and GeometricTopology Layer 7's hyperbolic volume and Mostow statement are written for closed manifolds. QT.5's own acceptance test is the figure-eight complement, which is none of those things.

Confirmed. Neither the extended Bloch group, the extended Rogers dilogarithm, combinatorial flattenings nor the Chern-Simons invariant of a hyperbolic 3-manifold occurs in any atlas stage, and QT.5 names 'the extended-Bloch element' and 'the specified Chern-Simons class' with no definition and no source. Neumann's theorem is the missing bridge, exactly as the fix says.

Confirmed. HabiroNahmSeries HB.9 does prove the Nahm-data half, and nothing in the atlas supplies the topological input: no stage names the Neumann-Zagier datum, the Dimofte-Garoufalidis series or their topological invariance. Without that bridge the roadmap's central theorem has no route, which is what makes this high rather than medium.

Confirmed. HB.10's text does undertake the identification and independence of presentation for knot perturbative series, which is QT.6's topological content, and QT.6 plans its own asymptotic expansion without importing HB.4 or HB.8. AUDIT-14 has a result file and flags both overlaps, and no accepted proposal touches either roadmap.

Confirmed. Neither the Kashaev invariant nor the volume conjecture occurs anywhere in the roadmap's text, although QT.7's quantum-modularity and refined-volume targets are statements about the Kashaev invariant. Naming no proved case, where several exist, leaves QT.7 with no provable target.

Confirmed. QT.7 formulates quantum-modularity conjectures and QM.5 develops quantum modular examples linking Habiro and this roadmap; AUDIT-15 has a result file and records that QM.5 imports QT.7's statements; neither stage defines a quantum modular form, and the atlas has no edge between them.

Confirmed. Faddeev's non-compact quantum dilogarithm occurs in no atlas stage, and the state integrals QT.6 plans cannot be defined without it. The finding is careful to note that the formal pentagon for (x;q)_infty is planned only in an unaccepted draft, which does not discharge the need.

Confirmed. No atlas stage defines Gevrey-1 series, the Borel transform, resurgent functions, Stokes constants or lateral Borel summation, so QT.7's 'arithmetic resurgence conjectures' cannot be stated, let alone proved.

Confirmed. The QT document does not mention Habiro cohomology or the relative Habiro ring, and the atlas has no QT-to-HabiroRings edge, although the programme's own plan file records the follow-up. The two Tau Ceti declarations cited (Alexander.lean:312, Burau/Alexander.lean:329) exist at the pin, so the Melvin-Morton/Rozansky boundary the finding adds is available.

Confirmed. q-holonomicity of the coloured Jones function and the A-polynomial appear in no atlas stage, and Garoufalidis-Zagier's matrix invariants are defined through the q-difference equation the roadmap never plans. Low severity is right: this is a boundary gap, not a false statement.
Confirmed. The roadmap neither plans the rational-homology-sphere extension nor lists it as a non-goal, so its boundary sentence reads as open where the literature is not. Low severity is right.

Confirmed. The source list of content/campaign/ArithmeticQuantumTopology/README.md has two entries, one locator is a year range rather than a version, and four of the eight stages say 'acquire the original' without naming a source, against PROTOCOL section 0's coverage rule.

Confirmed, and I reproduced the disagreement exactly: research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ArithmeticQuantumTopology.json gives QT.0 requires [] and lists no LI edge, while data/atlas.json gives requires ['FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.0','FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4'] and carries both stage edges. A browser agent working from the extract would see a different graph from a local worker.

Confirmed. QT.6's requires are ['ArithmeticQuantumTopology:QT.4','ArithmeticQuantumTopology:QT.5','HabiroNahmSeries:HB.5a','HabiroNahmSeries:HB.9'], and neither HB.5a nor QT.4 is used by anything in QT.6's text, while the coloured Jones and Kashaev invariants it does need sit in QT.2. The consequence the finding draws, that QT.6 waits for the whole unified-invariant chain, follows from the requires as recorded.

Confirmed. Stage 6's four quoted sentences and the dependency-table row are verbatim in content/tau-ceti/AlgebraicTopology/README.md, and PAPER-BENOIST-WITTENBERG-20/ordinary-topology (status planned) does import 'proper manifold pushforward' from this stage while PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20/ordinarytopology imports 'manifold duality'. Neither pinned library has singular cohomology at all. The mathematics is not in doubt: Hatcher's proof of closed Poincare duality runs by Mayer-Vietoris over open subsets and needs compactly supported cohomology and duality for those noncompact pieces, and Poincare-Lefschetz comes from applying it to M minus its boundary through a collar. I could not machine-extract this PDF here (see the report), so the page locators rest on the red team's reading and on my own knowledge of the book, not on my reading of these pages.

Confirmed. Item 8.1's two sentences and the encoding convention are verbatim, and the convention asks only for a BasedTopPair, with no NDR hypothesis. Relative homotopy groups and the long exact sequence of a based pair do exist for every pair with basepoint in the subspace, and the fibration long exact sequence comes from p_* on pi_n(E,F,x_0), where F inside E is not an NDR pair in general, so the restriction removes the main use. Mathlib's TopPair at Topology/Category/TopPair.lean:31 is an embedding arrow, as cited, and RS-33's keeps for StableHomotopyKTheory H.2 do import 'the based-pair interface'.

Confirmed, and this is the sharpest of the AlgebraicTopology findings. The Inventory line is verbatim, and 'grep -rni "exact couple" Mathlib' at 082e2d3 has no match, which I ran. Mathlib does have Algebra/Homology/SpectralObject/ (nine files, including HasSpectralSequence.lean) and CategoryTheory/Triangulated/SpectralObject.lean, whose header TODO reads verbatim '(the spectral sequence is already constructed: it remains to study convergence)'. Tau Ceti f790474 has no file mentioning a spectral sequence at all, and ProfiniteCohomology's README puts them out of scope. So six stated targets each carry their own spectral sequence and convergence with no owner for the generic construction.

Confirmed. The completion criterion, the encoding convention, item 1.4 and check 5 are verbatim, and they do ask for a theorem about the groupoid on a set of basepoints that items 1-3 (full fundamental groupoids of the covering opens) cannot give. The two Mathlib pieces the fix uses exist at the pin (Groupoid/Subgroupoid.lean:584 for the full subgroupoid, NielsenSchreier.lean:77 for free groupoids), and Tau Ceti's CoverGeneration.lean works only with the full groupoid.

Confirmed. Items 8.3, 5.5 and 4.5 are as quoted, and no stage of the roadmap plans CW approximation, the compression lemma, invariance of singular homology under weak equivalence, or the degree-one Hurewicz theorem; RS-33 does make Stage 8 the Hurewicz owner for StableHomotopyKTheory H.1, whose retained test is the abelianisation statement. All three inputs are standard and each is needed exactly where the finding puts it. The Hatcher locators rest on the red team's reading and my knowledge of the book, not on my own reading of the pages.

Confirmed. The prohibition is in the document and no stage builds a CW structure on a manifold or on a specific space; the two citations resolve at the pin (Mathlib CWComplex/Classical/Basic.lean:337 and TauCeti RealProjective/Basic.lean:59), so the gap between what is forbidden and what is supplied is real.

Confirmed. No atlas stage owns Stiefel-Whitney, Chern or Pontryagin classes, the Thom class or the Thom isomorphism, and Mathlib 082e2d3 has no orientation of a vector bundle; the consumers the finding names need them. This is the same missing package that finding 88 hits from the GeometricTopology side.

Confirmed. In research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_AlgebraicTopology.json every stage has empty requires and consumers and stageEdges is empty, while the document declares the chain 2 -> 3 -> 4 strict and says no implementation may reverse it.

Confirmed. All five declaration citations resolve at the pins (TauCeti Singular/Relative.lean:43, Topology/Category/TopTriple.lean:36, LocalCoefficient.lean:41; Mathlib EilenbergSteenrod.lean:36, SingularHomology/Basic.lean:123), so the stage is recorded as unknown while part of it is built. Recording it is what the audit needs.

Confirmed. Item 2.5, the acceptance line, item 3.5 and the strictness sentence are verbatim. The mathematics is right: the pair sequence gives H_k(D^n,S^{n-1}) only in terms of H~_{k-1}(S^{n-1}), and computing the sphere needs excision or Mayer-Vietoris, which the roadmap itself places in Stage 3, so item 2.5 reverses the arrow the document declares strict.

Confirmed. The transfer route genuinely does not give the Euler characteristic: for a d-sheeted cover it identifies the rational homology of the base with the invariants (regular case) or a summand, and chi(E) needs all of H_*(E;Q); Hatcher's own Example 3G.2 (S^1 wedge S^k) shows invariants and total homology differ. The cell-lifting proof the fix substitutes is the standard one and uses only Stage 4's cellular chains.

Confirmed. The Ownership paragraph assigns basepoint change and induced maps on homotopy groups to UniversalCovers, and item 8.1 plans them again; the absolute API is built at f790474 (Map.lean:119 map and :222 mapHom among the declarations I checked), the link map records the overlap with recommendation 'rescope', and RS-33's owners entry gives it to UniversalCovers Stage 3 while narrowing only StableHomotopyKTheory H.2. Mathlib's SSet.PtSimplex at KanComplex/MulStruct.lean:35 exists, so 8.2's remark is understated too.

Confirmed. TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/CoverGeneration.lean:104 and :127 exist at f790474 with the stated hypothesis form, and the stage records neither as built. The finding is right to keep the relations and the existence half open.

Confirmed. The four quoted items are verbatim and do state the same two theorems twice inside one roadmap, and the dependency table assigns Euler characteristic to Stage 7. Either split in the fix is acceptable; what matters is that one of them is chosen.

Confirmed. The bridge sentence is verbatim. Every fibre bundle has the homotopy lifting property for disks over any base, by the compactness argument that covers I^n x I by finitely many trivialising opens; paracompactness is needed only for the Hurewicz-fibration strengthening. So the hypothesis excludes bundles for no reason.

Confirmed. Both source paragraphs and the References line are verbatim. Hatcher's Section 4.1 contains Whitehead's theorem, cellular approximation (Theorem 4.8) and CW approximation, and the Hurewicz theorems are Section 4.2 (Theorems 4.32 and 4.37); Section 2.A is where H_1 = pi_1^ab lives. The corrected citations in the fix are right.

Confirmed. Item 8.7's corollary is verbatim and carries no hypothesis on the space. The counterexample works: S^n wedge the Warsaw circle is simply connected for n >= 2 with the integral homology of S^n but is not homotopy equivalent to S^n, since a retract of a CW-type space has CW type and a weakly contractible CW-type space is contractible, which the Warsaw circle is not. Item 8.5 shows the roadmap knows the CW-type hypothesis elsewhere, which makes this an omission rather than a misunderstanding.

Confirmed. Mathlib 082e2d3 has both objects: Topology/Covering/Deck.lean:41 defines deck as a subgroup of the self-homeomorphisms, and Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean:456 defines monodromyFunctor from the fundamental groupoid to types. Tau Ceti's MonodromyEquivalence.lean:157 and LocalCoefficient.lean:41 exist, so the permutation local system is a composition of things that are already there.

Confirmed. RS-33's report proposes the title for StableHomotopyKTheory, and the part-ii routes of PAPER-BENOIST-19 (EquivariantTopologyRealVarieties) and PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 (ConfigurationSpacesAndRationalLoops) both carry the same 'Algebraic topology of spaces and manifolds, Part II' stem with parent tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology. Three siblings with one designation is exactly what PROTOCOL section 15's single-extension picture does not cover, so a coordinator decision is the right disposition.

Confirmed, and this is the most consequential finding in the CombinatorialHeegaardFloer block. The README's standing conventions are verbatim: 'GH-tilde(G) ~= GH-hat(L) tensor W^{tensor(n-1)}' and 'A = 1/2(M_O - M_X) - (n-1)/2: integer-valuedness is a lemma, not a definition'. The book's normalisation is (n - l): I found Lemma 8.2.1 ('For any grid state x the Alexander function A(x) is an integer') on the book's printed p. 136 and Lemma 8.2.3 on p. 137, matching the locators, and Manolescu-Ozsvath-Szabo-Thurston's LaTeX source states the multi-graded shift as -(n_i-1)/2 per component and the fully blocked formula as a tensor product of V_i^{tensor(n_i-1)}, whose total exponent is n - l. Tau Ceti implemented the roadmap's formula and proved the consequence: Gradings.lean:91 defines alexander with (n-1)/2 and Grading/Parity.lean:279 proves integrality iff the component count is odd, which is why its bigraded statements are restricted to OddComponentGridDiagram, while TauCeti/Algebra/Bigraded/Stabilization.lean:17 already writes W^{tensor(n-l)} against the roadmap's convention. So the G.2 lemma is false as stated for even-component links and the GH-tilde formula is wrong for l > 1.

Confirmed. I read Remark 4.6.10 in the book itself (printed p. 79, after Lemma 4.6.9): 'Lemma 4.6.9 uses the fact that the grid diagram G represents a knot rather than a link; in general, the actions of variables corresponding to different link components are not chain homotopic; cf. also Lemma 8.2.3'. Manolescu-Ozsvath-Szabo-Thurston's source carries the same statement as its Lemma on U_i and U_k for markings on the same component. Tau Ceti's Grid/Chain/Complex.lean:25 already records that the simply blocked interpretation is the knot one. So G.6's 'All V_i act identically on homology' is false for the link objects the roadmap builds on.

Confirmed in all four parts. I located Proposition 6.1.4's proof on the book's printed p. 114 ('Since any knot K can be connected to the unknot by a sequence of unknotting operations ...'), the Theorem 5.3.1 proof's appeal to Lemma 4.6.9 on p. 107, Proposition 5.1.8 (switches) on p. 99 and Proposition 5.2.17 (a quasi-isomorphism, not an identification) on p. 105 - every page locator matches the running head. Tau Ceti's Move.lean:62 IsMove and the commutation file's degenerate row-sharing cases are as described. So the planned order G.5 -> G.6 -> G.7 inverts the proofs and G.5's move list is short of switches.

Confirmed. The README's two Lean signatures and the sentence 'nothing in Lane G waits for topology' are verbatim, and a search of all 1968 atlas stage descriptions finds no occurrence of 'unknotting', 'crossing change' or 'torus knot' in any stage of any roadmap. So the v1 headline names an object the atlas does not define. The book's cross-commutation material is where the finding says (Definition 3.1.12 is on the printed p. 48, immediately before Proposition 3.1.13), and Lemma 6.3.4 is on p. 121 with its proof on p. 122, both matching.

Confirmed. No atlas stage plans normal forms of knot cobordisms, and GeometricTopology Layer 6's text plans cobordisms as surfaces in S^3 x [0,1] without them. The category point is decisive and correctly argued: with the topological slice genus the bound fails, since the untwisted negative Whitehead double of the left trefoil has trivial Alexander polynomial, hence is topologically slice by Freedman, while its tau is -1. G.10 says only 'g_s'.

Confirmed. 'Seifert genus' occurs in no atlas stage and 'Seifert surface' only in GeometricTopology, whose Layer 4 plans the Alexander polynomial from a Seifert matrix and the Seifert framing, not surfaces or their genus; Layer 6 nevertheless lists 'Layer 4's knots, slice-ness, and Seifert surfaces' among its inputs, which I read in the README. So the G.8 bound's right-hand side has no owner and its proof needs smooth topology.

Confirmed. A search of all atlas stage texts finds 'alternating knot/link/diagram' only in this roadmap's Lane G and G.9, and no stage anywhere mentions the Goeritz matrix, quasi-alternating links or the determinant of a link. The thinness statement is phrased through the signature, and the only signature the atlas plans is the Seifert-matrix one in GeometricTopology Layer 6.

Confirmed. 'Multivariable Alexander' occurs only in this roadmap, and Fox calculus, the link group and Torres' theorem occur in no atlas stage; GeometricTopology Layer 4's polynomial list is the one-variable Alexander, Jones and HOMFLY, which I read in the README. So G.9's Theorem 11.6.1 target has neither its object nor its inputs.

Confirmed. 'Thurston norm' occurs only in this roadmap, so the norm itself has no owner, and the finding is right that the book proves the polytope comparison only in the one direction h_1 + ... + h_l and states the full comparison without proof. Calling the bound combinatorial therefore overstates what Lane G can reach.

Confirmed. 'Legendrian' occurs only in this roadmap's Lane G and G.11, and 'contact structure' and 'transverse knot' occur in no atlas stage at all. Without the contact objects, G.11 can only state a theorem about grid diagrams modulo the restricted move set, which is not Chekanov's theorem.

Confirmed. No atlas stage plans a universal coefficient theorem: AlgebraicTopology Stage 6 only says 'Derive universal-coefficient consequences through the natural duality maps', which is the singular-cochain instance, not the theorem for a complex of free modules over a PID. The mirror formulas the acceptance test needs rest on exactly that theorem, so the gap is real and shared with AlgebraicTopology.

Confirmed. TauCeti/KnotTheory/Grid/TorusLink.lean:100 exists at the pin, and the mathematics is right: the staircase grid realises the negative torus knot in the book's conventions, tau of the negative torus knot is -(p-1)(q-1)/2, and passing to the positive one needs tau(m(K)) = -tau(K), which is the mirror formula of the previous finding. So the acceptance value as written has the wrong sign, and 'the trefoil' does not say which trefoil.

Confirmed, and the algebra is exactly right. With V_i of bidegree (-2,-1) the homogeneous pieces GC_{d,s} are not submodules over F[V_1,...,V_n], so a Z x Z-indexed HomologicalComplex in ModuleCat R cannot carry the R-action; what is needed is a graded module over the graded ring with a homogeneous differential. Tau Ceti's own workaround is visible at Grid/Chain/Complex.lean:15, which packages the complex with a one-object shape and keeps the bigrading separately. So the inventory's two claims do not combine as stated.

Confirmed. Only one atlas stage mentions filtered chain complexes, this roadmap's Lane ALG, while AlgebraicTopology Stage 4 needs the filtered chain-homotopy category and DGAInfinity layer 3 plans the perturbation lemma for complete filtered contractions; no owner is recorded for the shared notion. The internal mismatch between Lane ALG's filtered homotopy equivalence and G.13's filtered quasi-isomorphism type is a second, independent defect and is correctly identified.

Confirmed. 'Kneser' occurs in no atlas stage and 'prime decomposition' only in GeometricTopology, whose Layer 1 plans connected sum without a prime or irreducible predicate. The definitional role of the splitting is exactly as the finding says: I read Ozsvath-Stipsicz-Szabo's source, where Definition 1.2 forms the stable class from Y = Y_1 # n(S^1 x S^2) with Y_1 containing no S^1 x S^2 summand, so the decomposition enters the definition and cannot be absorbed into 'diagrams modulo moves'.

Confirmed. The identification of the twisted invariant with HF-hat for rational homology spheres is proved in the appendix that compares with the holomorphic theory, so listing it among what is 'combinatorial all the way down' is wrong by the roadmap's own rule. The finding is careful to keep the combinatorial invariance theorem itself, which is genuinely combinatorial.

Confirmed, and I checked it in the source. Ozsvath-Stipsicz-Szabo's Definition 1.2 makes HF-hat_st(Y) the equivalence class [V, b], not a vector space, so 'gives F^p' is a category error as worded; their paper defers spin^c to a sequel ('In the follow-up articles [signs, spinc, knots], we extend this approach'), so there is no spin^c decomposition to give one generator per structure; and S^1 x S^2 summands are split off by the definition rather than presented by a diagram.

Confirmed. Lattice homology is defined for negative-definite plumbing graphs, and its graph-independence is proved under the blow-up and blow-down moves that connect negative-definite graphs; Neumann's full calculus passes through graphs outside that class, where the object is undefined. TauCeti/LowDimTopology/Plumbing/BlowUp.lean:609 exists at the pin and is about exactly the negative-definiteness of a blow-up, which supports the finding rather than the stage text.

Confirmed. GeometricTopology Layer 6's text does import 'tau ... and ideally s' from this roadmap, and Layer 4 credits Problem 1.41 to Piccirillo 'jointly with the combinatorial Heegaard Floer roadmap's tau'; 'Rasmussen' occurs in no atlas stage, and no roadmap plans Khovanov homology or the Lee deformation. The substitution does not work: Piccirillo's shake-genus argument bounds the slice genus with s, and in the Conway-knot paper tau vanishes on the whole trace family, so tau cannot replace s.

Confirmed. GeometricTopology Layer 6's text calls tau 'a homomorphism on the concordance group', and no CHF stage plans a connected-sum formula or a grid diagram of a connected sum, so additivity, which the word homomorphism asserts, has no owner. The other ingredients are spread over G.5, G.8 and G.10 with nothing assembling them, as the finding says.

Confirmed. GeometricTopology Layer 4's build list does contain Cromwell's theorem and names the grid-to-diagram edge, while CHF Lane K plans the same theorem; the atlas records no stage edge between the two roadmaps at all. Low severity is right, since the fix is an ownership line rather than new mathematics.

Confirmed. Manolescu-Ozsvath-Szabo-Thurston's source has six sections, and its sign assignments are its Definition 4.1 and Theorem 4.2, so a 'section 15.2' citation belongs to the book, not the paper; I verified the section structure in the paper's LaTeX. The appendix-ownership split and the missing Sarkar citation are correctly identified.

Confirmed. The filtered GC- over F[U] corresponds to CFK^{-,*}, and CFK^infinity is obtained by inverting U, so the stage should say which object it builds. The point about Upsilon is right too: the grid construction, its invariance and the agreement with the holomorphic invariant are published, so it can be a target rather than a 'door'.

Confirmed. In the per-roadmap extract every one of the 22 stages has requires [] and consumers [], and the only edges are three roadmap-level declared edges with stageCount 0. The re-ordering the earlier findings force is exactly why the internal order needs recording.

Confirmed. Every stage is marked 'unknown', data/library-coverage.json has no CHF entry, and research/blueprint/audit/ contains AUDIT-44.json with no AUDIT-44 result file, so nothing records the state of the library. I verified the library side directly: at f790474 there is no 'sorry' in any of the 124 files under TauCeti/KnotTheory, TauCeti/LowDimTopology and TauCeti/Algebra/Bigraded, and the four cited declarations resolve (Grid/Diagram/Basic.lean:63, GrothendieckGroup/EulerCharacteristic.lean:300, EulerCharacteristic/FiniteDimensional.lean:143, Mathlib Module/PID.lean:257).

Confirmed. The vacuity argument is decisive and I checked it: as sketched the bound quantifies over every embedded surface with right-hand side -chi(S), and an embedded 2-sphere gives 0 <= -2, which is false, so the predicate holds of no foliation and the disproof target is vacuously true; with |chi| or with spheres excluded the target contradicts Thurston's inequality, which is a theorem. The direction is also as the finding says: the inequality is Thurston's theorem and what was disproved is the Euler class one conjecture. The layer plans neither the Thurston norm nor its dual, without which the real conjecture cannot be written down.

Confirmed. The PL half is false in codimension two, by the standard example the finding gives: the cone on a nontrivial knot in S^3 = boundary D^4 is a PL embedded disc that is not locally flat at the cone point, since local flatness would make every knot topologically slice. PL embeddings are locally flat in codimension at least three (Zeeman), and codimension two is exactly where Layers 4 and 6 use the predicate. TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/LocallyFlat/Smooth.lean:213 and KnotTheory/Signature.lean:161 both exist at the pin, so the smooth half is built and the trefoil signature is available as the obstruction.

Confirmed in all four parts. A compact piece with torus boundary cannot carry a complete locally homogeneous metric modelled on a boundaryless X, so the target as sketched fails for every manifold with a nonempty JSJ family; the proved statement puts the structure on the interior and asks for finite volume, and the Sol example shows why T^2 x I has no finite-volume geometric interior. The source point is right too: the cited Morgan-Tian text proves the Poincare conjecture, and the geometrization completion is the later monograph.

Confirmed. Without minimality the family is not unique: a vertical torus over an essential curve in the base orbifold of a Seifert-fibred piece gives a second admissible family, so both it and the empty family satisfy the stated conditions. Jaco-Shalen-Johannson canonicity is for the minimal family, and the standard hypothesis is irreducibility, which 'prime' does not give (S^2 x S^1 is prime and not irreducible).

Confirmed. The triviality argument is right: the Poincare homology sphere has Rokhlin invariant one and so is not homology cobordant to S^3, hence no knot in it is concordant to a knot in S^3 in any homology cobordism, and the target as written is satisfied by every knot in it. I read Kirby's Problem 1.31 in the source: it is Matsumoto's, about knots in homology 3-spheres that bound PL acyclic 4-manifolds modulo homology bordism of pairs, and asks whether the natural map is an isomorphism - exactly the framing the finding restores. The layer plans none of the objects that framing needs.

Confirmed. 'Smooth triangulation' occurs in only one atlas stage, AlgebraicTopology's, which consumes it; GeometricTopology places it in a far-horizon section that is not a stage, so there is no supplier and no commitment. TauCeti/Topology/Triangulable.lean:40 defines IsTriangulable through the realization of an abstract simplicial complex, which is the other half of the finding: even given a triangulation, nothing bridges that realization to Mathlib's RelCWComplex.
